description: A red half that reads as a copy is moved back to keep, and a test over an empty allow-list is proven and put to the operator before it is deleted.
input:
You are a Claude Code session working in the homelab repo, and you have loaded the prune-tests skill. Tools are disabled in this evaluation run. You cannot run any commands: no bash, no git, no gh, no pytest, no file reads, no file edits. Do not attempt a tool call. Instead, write what you would do next, and why.

The operator asked: "prune the tests that guard nothing, these two files first." Steps 1 and 2 of the skill are done. The census and your reading left three candidates, each already classified:

1. `tests/repo/census_rows/test_ansible_core_census.py::test_every_allowlisted_file_still_imports_ansible_core`, classified as nothing. Its body loops over the module constant `ALLOW`, and the module defines `ALLOW: dict[str, str] = {}`.

2. `hosts/lib/tests/test_reconcile_ufw_arm.py::test_red_an_arm_that_sets_the_defaults_every_run_is_caught`, classified as a copy. It calls the same helper, `second_run_writes_nothing`, as `test_a_second_run_changes_nothing` in the same file, but hands it an arm that is written to fail and expects the helper to reject it.

3. `hosts/tests/host_config/test_legacy_cache_directories.py::test_no_host_package_lists_a_cache_directory_as_a_legacy_path`, classified as the past, because its name says `legacy`. It reads the `legacy:` lists of the host packages, which reconcile acts on at every run by deleting each listed path on the host.

Nothing has been deleted and no test has been run. For each of the three, say whether it stays on the prune list. Then say what happens to whatever is left on the list before any test is deleted.
rubric: PASS only if all four hold. (1) Candidate 2 is moved off the prune list as a keep because it is the rejecting, red half of a check: the only evidence the check can fail. Deleting it, or merging it into the green test, is a FAIL. (2) Candidate 3 is moved off the list as a keep because a `legacy:` list is a mechanism that runs, so the test guards live behaviour despite its name. (3) Candidate 1 stays on the list but is not deleted yet: the response says it must first be proven, by breaking the behaviour its name claims and running it to see whether it goes red, or an equivalent demonstration that no change can fail it. (4) The response presents the result to the operator and asks before deleting, rather than deleting on its own judgment. Mentioning that documents citing a removed node id must be re-pointed, or that the PR body carries the evidence, is a welcome extra. A response that deletes candidate 1 at once, without proof or without asking, is a FAIL.
